name: LAZARUS PHARMACEUTICALS NeuroPrecision Surgical Control Suit
description:
The NeuroPrecision Surgical Control Suite is a medical-grade BCI platform developed by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals in collaboration with the Meridian 88 College of Surgical Sciences. The implant interfaces with the motor cortex and cerebellum simultaneously, using a 512-channel electrode array to intercept, filter, and re-amplify efferent motor signals before they reach the peripheral nervous system. A dedicated tremor-cancellation co-processor running at 4kHz samples hand and wrist motor commands in real time, applying adaptive inverse-frequency dampening to eliminate physiological tremor down to 0.003mm positional variance. The suite also includes a haptic-feedback upscaling layer that amplifies tactile sensation from surgical instruments by a factor of 40x, allowing surgeons to detect tissue resistance gradients that are imperceptible to unaugmented practitioners. A secondary neural thread handles intraoperative AR overlay, projecting patient vitals, imaging data, and instrument telemetry directly onto the surgical field as perceived by the user.

The NeuroPrecision is the de facto standard implant for licensed surgeons operating within Meridian 88's Tier 3 and 4 hospital networks, particularly those affiliated with Lazarus Pharmaceuticals' own MedCenter chain. First-year surgical residents are frequently issued the implant on deferred-payment employer plans, with the understanding that the hardware includes a soft compliance lock — surgeons who leave Lazarus-affiliated institutions within five years of implantation face a licensing throttle that reduces tremor-cancellation fidelity to 60% until the device is re-keyed by a certified Lazarus technician. This practice is widely criticized by independent medical ethicists but remains technically legal under Meridian 88's Professional Tools Retention Statute. Among surgical staff, the implant is affectionately called 'Lazarus Locks' — both for the performance it provides and for the contractual chains it represents.
installation_requirements: Neurosurgical implantation by Lazarus-certified installer; pre-op MRI mapping of motor cortex required; 72-hour calibration hospitalization; annual re-certification by licensed Lazarus technician
rejection_risk: Low — biocompatible polymer electrode array with anti-inflammatory slow-release coating; elevated risk in patients with pre-existing cerebellar lesions
maintenance: Quarterly firmware calibration; annual electrode impedance check; co-processor battery cell replacement every 18 months; Lazarus MedCenter service contract strongly recommended

side_effects: Hypersensitivity syndrome — augmented haptic feedback occasionally bleeds into daily life, making ordinary textures and surfaces feel overwhelming or distressing
Motor signal dependency — some long-term users report difficulty performing fine motor tasks without the implant active, as the brain partially delegates precision movement to the co-processor
Intraoperative dissociation — a small percentage of users report a detached, observer-like psychological state during procedures, attributed to the implant's interception of proprioceptive feedback
Compliance lock anxiety — documented psychological stress responses in surgeons approaching contract end dates, tied to anticipated fidelity throttling
cultural_context: In Meridian 88's medical community, the NeuroPrecision has become a symbol of the blurring line between professional tool and corporate leash. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals markets it as 'the gift of a steady hand,' and the implant genuinely transforms surgical outcomes — mortality rates in NeuroPrecision-assisted procedures are 23% lower than unaugmented equivalents according to Lazarus's own published data. But the compliance lock provision has spawned a shadow industry of third-party re-keying services operating out of Tier 2 clinics, where surgeons who have left Lazarus networks pay black-market technicians to unlock their own neural hardware. The ethical debate around employer-locked medical implants is one of the most active political flashpoints in the city's professional labor movement.
known_users: Licensed surgeons at Lazarus MedCenter hospitals and affiliated Tier 3-4 clinics
Neurosurgical residents on Lazarus deferred-payment employer plans
Specialist trauma surgeons in Meridian 88's emergency response networks
Private practice surgeons serving Tier 4-5 clientele
story_hooks: A brilliant independent surgeon approaches the party — she left a Lazarus MedCenter two years ago and her compliance lock is throttling her precision. A child needs a surgery only she can perform, but she needs someone to get her to a black-market re-keying tech before the operating window closes.

A Lazarus Pharmaceuticals internal whistleblower has evidence that a firmware update pushed to all NeuroPrecision units last month contains a new feature — a remote kill switch that can induce full motor seizure in the implanted surgeon. They need help getting the evidence out before Lazarus's security division finds them.

The party is hired to recover a stolen NeuroPrecision calibration key from a corporate espionage operative — but the key belongs to a surgeon currently mid-operation at a Tier 4 hospital, and without re-keying within six hours, the compliance lock will engage and the patient on the table will die.
